nodes.name: Babylonian arithmetic
nodes.description: Sexagesimal place-value arithmetic on clay tablets, with tables of reciprocals, squares and Pythagorean triples.

nodes.name: Egyptian surveying
nodes.description: Practical rules for areas and volumes, used for land measurement after Nile floods.
results: Volume of a truncated pyramid (Moscow papyrus)

nodes.name: Pythagorean number theory
nodes.description: Numbers studied for their own sake: parity, figurate numbers, ratios, and the shock of incommensurability.

nodes.name: Syllogistic logic
nodes.description: Aristotle's formal theory of valid inference from premises. The ancestor of all later logic.
results: Law of the excluded middle stated explicitly

nodes.name: Euclidean geometry
nodes.description: The Elements organize geometry and arithmetic as deductions from a few axioms. The template for proof for two millennia.

nodes.name: Method of exhaustion
nodes.description: Eudoxus and Archimedes bound areas and volumes between inscribed and circumscribed figures. Integration without limits.

nodes.name: Conic sections
nodes.description: Apollonius's synthetic study of ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas as sections of a cone.
results: Names and classification of the conics

nodes.name: The Nine Chapters
nodes.description: China's Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art: a handbook of 246 problems on surveying, taxation and engineering, with general algorithms.
results: Fangcheng: elimination on rectangular arrays (Gaussian elimination)

nodes.name: Indian combinatorics
nodes.description: Pingala counts the possible patterns of long and short syllables in Sanskrit verse, and later scholars extend his rules.

nodes.name: Trigonometry
nodes.description: Hipparchus's chord tables, Ptolemy's Almagest, then the Indian sine. Geometry made computable for astronomy.

nodes.name: Diophantine analysis
nodes.description: Diophantus's Arithmetica seeks rational solutions to polynomial equations, using an early syncopated notation.
results: Rational points on conics and cubics
The margin in which Fermat later wrote

nodes.name: Maya zero
nodes.description: The Maya Long Count calendar uses a true positional zero in a base-20 system, found entirely apart from the Old World.
results: Venus tables in the Dresden Codex

nodes.name: Place value & zero
nodes.description: Brahmagupta treats zero and negatives as numbers with arithmetic rules. Decimal place value spreads west.
results: Rules for arithmetic with zero and negatives

nodes.name: Al-jabr
nodes.description: Al-Khwarizmi's systematic solution of linear and quadratic equations by completion and balancing.

nodes.name: Kerala series
nodes.description: Madhava's school finds infinite series for π, sine and arctangent, centuries before Europe.
results: Power series for sin and cos

nodes.name: Cubic & quartic
nodes.description: Del Ferro, Tartaglia, Cardano and Ferrari solve degree 3 and 4 by radicals.

nodes.name: Complex numbers
nodes.description: Bombelli takes √−1 seriously because Cardano's formula needs it to reach real roots.

nodes.name: Symbolic algebra
nodes.description: Viète uses letters for knowns and unknowns alike, making equations objects that can be manipulated.

nodes.name: Logarithms
nodes.description: Napier and Bürgi turn multiplication into addition. Bürgi's version was found independently.

nodes.name: Analytic geometry
nodes.description: Descartes and Fermat, independently, put coordinates on the plane: curves become equations.

nodes.name: Projective geometry
nodes.description: Desargues studies what survives perspective projection. Ignored for nearly two centuries, then revived by Poncelet in 1822.

nodes.name: Probability
nodes.description: Pascal and Fermat's letters on the problem of points turn games of chance into mathematics.

nodes.name: Newton's fluxions
nodes.description: Newton's calculus of flowing quantities, built for mechanics and kept mostly unpublished for decades.

nodes.name: Combinatorics
nodes.description: Leibniz's Dissertatio de arte combinatoria and Bernoulli's work on permutations make counting a European subject.

nodes.name: Leibniz's calculus
nodes.description: Leibniz's independent calculus, with the d and ∫ notation that won.

nodes.name: Celestial mechanics
nodes.description: Newton's Principia derives Kepler's elliptical orbits from an inverse-square law. Apollonius's conics turn out to be the shapes of orbits.

nodes.name: Differential equations
nodes.description: The Bernoullis, Euler and Lagrange turn physical laws into equations for unknown functions.

nodes.name: Numerical analysis
nodes.description: Approximation as a discipline: methods to compute answers you cannot write down, with control of the error.

nodes.name: Calculus of variations
nodes.description: Born from Johann Bernoulli's brachistochrone challenge: find the curve, not the point, that optimizes.

nodes.name: Graph theory
nodes.description: Euler's Königsberg bridges: a problem where only connections matter, not distances.

nodes.name: Partial differential equations
nodes.description: D'Alembert writes the wave equation for a vibrating string; physics becomes a matter of fields governed by PDEs.

nodes.name: Analysis of functions
nodes.description: Euler's Introductio makes the function, not the curve, the central object, and handles infinite series with abandon.
results: e^{ix} = cos x + i sin x

nodes.name: Bayesian inference
nodes.description: Bayes's posthumous essay reverses probability: from effects back to causes. Laplace found the rule again independently in 1774.

nodes.name: Modern number theory
nodes.description: From Fermat's marginalia through Euler to Gauss's Disquisitiones Arithmeticae: congruences and quadratic forms.

nodes.name: Fourier analysis
nodes.description: Fourier claims any function is a sum of sines, to solve the heat equation. The claim forced analysis to become rigorous.

nodes.name: Mathematical statistics
nodes.description: Gauss and Laplace fit models to noisy observations: least squares and the normal law of errors.

nodes.name: Rigorous analysis
nodes.description: Cauchy, Bolzano and Weierstrass rebuild calculus on limits and ε–δ, purging infinitesimals.

nodes.name: Complex analysis
nodes.description: Cauchy's contour integrals and Riemann's geometric view: calculus over the complex plane is unexpectedly rigid and beautiful.

nodes.name: Differential geometry
nodes.description: Gauss studies curved surfaces from the inside, discovering curvature is intrinsic.

nodes.name: Lobachevsky's geometry
nodes.description: Lobachevsky publishes a consistent geometry in which the parallel postulate fails.

nodes.name: Bolyai's geometry
nodes.description: János Bolyai independently reaches the same non-Euclidean geometry. Gauss had found it privately and never published.

nodes.name: Group theory
nodes.description: Galois explains which polynomials are solvable by radicals by studying symmetries of their roots.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian mechanics
nodes.description: Hamilton restates mechanics as a flow on phase space, a form that later carries over to quantum theory.

nodes.name: Analytic number theory
nodes.description: Dirichlet and then Riemann attack primes with the tools of analysis: a hybrid of two distant lineages.
results: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions

nodes.name: Quaternions
nodes.description: Hamilton carves i² = j² = k² = ijk = −1 into Brougham Bridge: the first number system where multiplication does not commute.
results: Dot and cross product (via Gibbs and Heaviside)

nodes.name: Linear algebra
nodes.description: Grassmann's extension theory and Cayley's matrices: vector spaces and linear maps as objects of study.

nodes.name: Invariant theory
nodes.description: Cayley and Sylvester compute polynomials unchanged under linear substitutions. Hilbert's 1890 proofs ended the computational era, and the field went quiet.

nodes.name: Boolean logic
nodes.description: Boole writes reasoning as algebra: propositions become variables, and logic becomes calculation.

nodes.name: Algebraic number theory
nodes.description: Kummer's ideal numbers rescue unique factorization in cyclotomic integers; Dedekind turns them into ideals.
results: Kummer's proof of Fermat for regular primes

nodes.name: Riemannian geometry
nodes.description: Riemann's Habilitation lecture: space of any dimension with a variable metric. Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry become special cases.
results: Later: the geometry of general relativity

nodes.name: Knot theory
nodes.description: Kelvin guesses atoms are knotted vortices; Tait tabulates knots to build a periodic table. The physics failed but the mathematics stayed.

nodes.name: Lie groups & algebras
nodes.description: Sophus Lie seeks a Galois theory for differential equations and finds continuous symmetry groups.
results: Lie's correspondence between groups and algebras
Killing–Cartan classification of simple Lie algebras

nodes.name: Set theory
nodes.description: Cantor's study of where Fourier series can fail leads him to infinite sets and different sizes of infinity.

nodes.name: Mathematical logic
nodes.description: Frege's Begriffsschrift introduces quantifiers and a formal language precise enough for all of mathematics.

nodes.name: Algebraic geometry
nodes.description: Solution sets of polynomial equations, studied by the Italian school, Hilbert and Noether. Geometry and algebra fully interbred.

nodes.name: Dynamical systems
nodes.description: Poincaré's three-body work studies the shape of all solutions rather than formulas for one. Chaos followed (Lorenz, 1963).

nodes.name: Algebraic topology
nodes.description: Poincaré's Analysis Situs attaches groups to spaces to tell them apart. Euler's graphs, Riemann's surfaces and Galois's groups all feed in.

nodes.name: Representation theory
nodes.description: Frobenius studies groups by how they act as matrices, turning abstract symmetry into linear algebra.

nodes.name: p-adic numbers
nodes.description: Hensel completes the rationals with respect to divisibility by a prime, making a separate calculus for each prime.

nodes.name: Tensor calculus
nodes.description: Ricci-Curbastro and Levi-Civita's absolute differential calculus: coordinate-free bookkeeping for curved space.

nodes.name: Measure theory
nodes.description: Lebesgue measures far wilder sets than Riemann could, giving an integral that commutes with limits.

nodes.name: Functional analysis
nodes.description: Hilbert, Fréchet, Riesz and Banach treat functions as points in infinite-dimensional spaces.

nodes.name: Markov chains
nodes.description: Markov extends the law of large numbers to dependent events, testing it on the vowels in Pushkin's Eugene Onegin.

nodes.name: Intuitionism
nodes.description: Brouwer rejects the law of excluded middle for infinite sets: to exist is to be constructed. Marginal for decades, it returns in type theory.

nodes.name: Axiomatic set theory
nodes.description: Zermelo axiomatizes sets to escape Russell's paradox; with Fraenkel's additions, ZFC becomes the default foundation of mathematics.

nodes.name: Point-set topology
nodes.description: Hausdorff axiomatizes open sets, giving continuity its most general home.

nodes.name: General relativity
nodes.description: Einstein models gravity as the curvature of spacetime. Riemann's geometry, built with no application in mind, turns out to describe gravity.

nodes.name: Complex dynamics
nodes.description: Fatou and Julia independently study iteration of rational maps of the complex plane, competing for the same prize.

nodes.name: Abstract algebra
nodes.description: Emmy Noether shifts algebra from calculation to structure: rings, ideals and modules.

nodes.name: Elliptic curves
nodes.description: Cubic curves whose rational points form a group. Mordell proves that group is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Brownian motion
nodes.description: Bachelier (1900, stock prices) and Einstein (1905, pollen grains) model random motion independently; Wiener makes it rigorous.

nodes.name: Game theory
nodes.description: Von Neumann proves the minimax theorem, making strategic conflict a mathematical subject.

nodes.name: Ramsey theory
nodes.description: Frank Ramsey, working on a problem in logic, proves complete disorder is impossible: large structures always contain order.

nodes.name: Incompleteness
nodes.description: Gödel shows any consistent formal system containing arithmetic has true but unprovable statements.

nodes.name: Quantum mechanics
nodes.description: Von Neumann puts quantum theory on Hilbert spaces: states are vectors, observables are self-adjoint operators.
results: Uncertainty principle as an operator inequality

nodes.name: Axiomatic probability
nodes.description: Kolmogorov grounds probability in measure theory. Three axioms, and a centuries-old field becomes rigorous.

nodes.name: Model theory
nodes.description: Tarski defines truth in a structure; logic becomes a tool for studying algebraic and geometric structures.

nodes.name: Lambda calculus
nodes.description: Church defines effective calculability via function abstraction and application.

nodes.name: Turing machines
nodes.description: Turing reaches the same limits independently, with an imagined machine. The two definitions turn out equivalent.

nodes.name: Finite element method
nodes.description: Courant splits a domain into small pieces and solves PDEs on each; engineers adopt it for bridges and aircraft.

nodes.name: Stochastic calculus
nodes.description: Itô defines integrals against Brownian motion, giving calculus for systems driven by noise.

nodes.name: Category theory
nodes.description: Eilenberg and Mac Lane invent a language for 'natural' maps between constructions in algebraic topology.

nodes.name: Sheaf theory
nodes.description: Leray, a prisoner of war, invents sheaves to track how local data patches together into global data.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo methods
nodes.description: Ulam, recovering from illness and playing solitaire, proposes estimating hard quantities by random sampling; von Neumann codes it for ENIAC.
results: Error falls as 1/√N regardless of dimension

nodes.name: Linear programming
nodes.description: Dantzig's simplex method optimizes over polytopes. Kantorovich had found the idea in 1939, unnoticed in the West.

nodes.name: Probabilistic method
nodes.description: Erdős proves objects exist by showing a random one works with positive probability, without constructing one.
results: Exponential lower bound for Ramsey numbers

nodes.name: Information theory
nodes.description: Shannon quantifies information as entropy, built from probability and Boolean switching circuits.

nodes.name: Coding theory
nodes.description: Hamming, annoyed by weekend job failures, builds codes that correct their own errors using finite fields.

nodes.name: Automata & formal languages
nodes.description: Kleene's regular expressions and Chomsky's grammar hierarchy classify machines by the languages they can recognize.

nodes.name: Gauge theory
nodes.description: Yang and Mills generalize electromagnetism to non-abelian symmetry groups. Physicists later learn it is the geometry of fiber bundles.

nodes.name: Homological algebra
nodes.description: Cartan and Eilenberg extract the algebraic machinery of homology so it can run anywhere.

nodes.name: Differential topology
nodes.description: Milnor finds a 7-dimensional sphere with a different smooth structure: smoothness is more than shape.

nodes.name: Schemes
nodes.description: Grothendieck rebuilds algebraic geometry on commutative rings and categories, unifying it with number theory.

nodes.name: Forcing & independence
nodes.description: Cohen invents forcing to show the continuum hypothesis cannot be proved from ZFC. Gödel had shown it cannot be disproved.
results: Independence of the axiom of choice

nodes.name: Topos theory
nodes.description: Grothendieck's toposes, built for geometry, turn out (Lawvere, 1970) to be universes for logic with their own internal mathematics.

nodes.name: Geometric invariant theory
nodes.description: Mumford revives classical invariant theory inside scheme theory to construct moduli spaces. A dormant lineage returns.

nodes.name: Langlands program
nodes.description: Langlands's letter to Weil conjectures a vast dictionary between number theory, representation theory and geometry.

nodes.name: Computational complexity
nodes.description: Cook and Levin define NP-completeness: not what can be computed, but what can be computed efficiently.

nodes.name: Statistical learning theory
nodes.description: Vapnik and Chervonenkis ask when learning from examples generalizes. Machine learning grows from this root.

nodes.name: Type theory & proof assistants
nodes.description: Martin-Löf's dependent types, descended from lambda calculus, become the foundation of Coq and Lean.

nodes.name: Mathematical finance
nodes.description: Black, Scholes and Merton price options by eliminating risk with a hedge, reducing the problem to a heat equation.

nodes.name: Fractal geometry
nodes.description: Mandelbrot names and popularizes self-similar sets with fractional dimension, drawn by early computers.

nodes.name: Public-key cryptography
nodes.description: Diffie–Hellman and RSA base secrecy on hard number-theoretic problems. GCHQ had found the same ideas in secret in 1970–73.

nodes.name: Quantum topology
nodes.description: Jones finds a new knot invariant inside von Neumann algebras; Witten explains it with quantum field theory.

nodes.name: Symplectic geometry
nodes.description: The geometry of phase space. Gromov's pseudo-holomorphic curves turn it into a modern field.

nodes.name: Fermat's Last Theorem
nodes.description: Wiles, with Taylor, proves enough of the modularity conjecture to settle Fermat's 358-year-old claim. Three centuries of lineages meet here.
results: xⁿ + yⁿ = zⁿ has no positive solutions for n > 2

nodes.name: Geometrization & Poincaré
nodes.description: Perelman proves Thurston's geometrization conjecture with Hamilton's Ricci flow, settling the Poincaré conjecture after a century.
